note: Errata ruling 26. Verbs left in three columns, inventory right as a scrollable list of item NAMES IN TEXT, sentence line full width above both -- the 1990 original's layout, and text inventory is the period-correct answer rather than a compromise. Geometry lives here rather than in Screen.ts because two things read it: the engine, and the Python that renders the panel for review. Two copies of a rectangle stay in agreement for about one commit.

verbs.note: SCUMM had twelve verbs in three columns of four. We have nine, per Bible v2, so the fourth row carries the MENU button instead of three more verbs -- the grid is the reference's shape and no cell is left empty.

inventory.note: Four rows visible, which is the bottom of ruling 26's four-to-six. Six would need 7px rows and the font is 7 tall, leaving no gap between names. The text column is 121px, which is twenty glyphs at the 5x7 advance -- that number is the truncation rule's whole basis.

arrows.note: Drawn as triangles, not typed. The 5x7 face has no arrow glyph and adding one would put an interface shape into the writing font.
